attributes.name: Duration of Response for Participants With Unconfirmed Response (CR+PR)
attributes.definition: Time from the first documented CR or PR until disease progression (PD)

attributes.text: Duration of response is defined as the time from the first documented CR (the disappearance of all detectable clinical and radiographic evidence of disease and all disease-related symptoms) or PR (greater than or equal to a 50% decrease in the SPPD determined at Baseline; no increase in the size of the other nodes, liver, or spleen; no new sites of disease) until disease progression (PD). PD is defined as greater than or equal to a 50% increase from nadir in the SPPD for all measurable disease.

attributes.name: Duration of Response (DOR) in Unconfirmed Complete Responders
attributes.definition: Time from the first documented response to the first documented disease progression

attributes.text: DOR is defined as the time from the first documented response to the first documented disease progression. CR is defined as the disappearance of all detectable clinical and radiographic evidence of disease and all disease-related symptoms. A confirmed response (CR and PR) requires that the response be confirmed by another response (same or better) at least 4 weeks apart.

attributes.name: Time to Progression or Death

attributes.text: Time to progression is defined as the time from the treatment start date to the first documented incidence of disease progression (PD) or death. PD is defined as greater than or equal to a 50% increase from nadir in the SPPD for all measurable disease. Lesion changes believed to represent measurement variation associated with radiographic technique should not be classified as PD.

attributes.name: Urine pH on Day 14 of Each Treatment Period

attributes.text: Urine samples were collected for the measurement of urine pH by dipstick method at Day 14. Urine pH is an acid-base measurement. pH is measured on a numeric scale ranging from 0 to 14; values on the scale refer to the degree of alkalinity or acidity. A pH of 7 is neutral. A pH less than 7 is acidic, and a pH greater than 7 is basic. Normal urine has a slightly acid pH (5.0 - 6.0).

attributes.name: Urine Specific Gravity on Day 14 of Each Treatment Period

attributes.text: Urine samples were collected for the measurement of urine specific gravity by dipstick method at Day 14. Urine specific gravity is a measure of the concentration of solutes in the urine and provides information on the kidney's ability to concentrate urine. The concentration of the excreted molecules determines the urine's specific gravity. A urinary specific gravity measurement is a routine part of urinalysis. The reference range is 1.002-1.030.

attributes.name: Mixed-Effects Model
attributes.description: {"transformation": "log-transformed", "fixed_effects": ["sequence", "treatment", "period"], "random_effects": "subject nested within sequence", "confidence_interval": "90% CI for treatment differences, 95% CI for least squares means", "bioequivalence_criteria": "80.00% to 125.00%"}

attributes.text: The primary endpoints, Cmax and AUC0-t in fasting or fed group, will be log-transformed and a mixed-effects model will be applied. The model will include fixed effects for sequence, treatment, and period and a random effect of subject nested within sequence. Treatment differences on the log scale will be estimated for the parameters together with their 90% CIs. The least squares means together with their 95% CIs by treatment will also be estimated. Point estimates and CIs will be back-transformed to the original scale for presentation, i.e., ratios of geometric means and corresponding 90% CIs for Treatment A/Treatment B, geometric means and corresponding 95% CIs by treatment, respectively.
The mixed trapezoidal rule will be used to calculate the area under the plasma concentration curve.
Pharmacokinetic parameters (primary and secondary endpoints) will be calculated according to non-compartmental analysis methods.
For tmax, the Hodges-Lehmann estimates for the treatment differences and corresponding 90% CIs according to the Tukey method will be calculated.

Terminal elimination rate constant. Determined from the terminal slope of the log-transformed concentration curve using linear regression on terminal data points of the curve. The regression analysis should contain data from at least 3 different time points in the terminal phase consistent with the assessment of a straight line on the log-transformed scale. Phoenix WinNonlin best fit methodology will be used as standard. The Rsq should be ≥0.800 and the observation period over which the regression line is estimated should be at least two-fold the resulting t1/2 itself.

attributes.text: The primary analysis will compare intervention groups (water supplementation vs control treatment) on their mean change in fasting plasma glucose between baseline and 12 months using a linear mixed model. Difference in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to time points where it is measured during the study (6 and 12 months) will be the dependent variable. Study subjects will be considered as random effects, treatment group and visit number as fixed effects. Baseline value of fasting plasma glucose will be included as a covariate. The estimated difference in mean change from baseline to 12 months and the corresponding 95 % confidence interval (CI) will be presented.
Cardiometabolic risk factors will be analysed using the same method as for the primary outcome, including usage of the baseline value for the actual factor as a covariate.
Diabetes incidence will be analysed using logistic regression, the odds ratio (OR) including 95 % CI will be presented.
In addition, correlation(s) between change in copeptin and change in cardiometabolic risk factors, other blood laboratory parameters and urine laboratory parameters may be calculated.

attributes.name: Primary Composite Endpoint
attributes.definition: Composite of procedural failure and 1-year target vessel failure, including: (1) Failed or no stent delivery determined by the angiographic core laboratory, (2) OCT-assessed residual area stenosis ≥20%, and (3) Target vessel failure within one year

attributes.text: The primary composite endpoint is determined by the following: • Failed or no stent delivery determined by the angiographic core laboratory. Failed or no stent delivery is defined as failure to deliver and deploy 1 or more coronary stents to cover the intended length of the intended target lesion. • OCT-assessed residual area stenosis ≥20%. Residual area stenosis is defined as 1 -[in-stent minimal lumen area (MLA) / reference lumen area]. Residual area stenosis will be determined primarily by OCT, or, if necessary, by quantitative coronary angiography, as defined in the OCT and quantitative coronary angiography definitions section of the protocol. The use of angiography is a form of imputation and we will investigate the impact of this in Section 7.1.2. • Target vessel failure within one year. Defined as cardiac death, target vessel-related myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target vessel revascularization.

For continuous outcomes we will use linear regression adjusting for site.

The primary analysis of efficacy will be performed using the ITT population. The change from baseline to in PDSS will be compared between HB-1 and placebo using Mixed Model Repeated Measures (MMRM) model using SAS mixed procedure with repeated measures. The model will include the fixed effect of treatment, visit, the treatment-by-visit interaction, baseline, baseline-by-visit. The outcome will be the change from baseline to each on-treatment time point. All protocol-scheduled time points will be included in the model. The model will use the unstructured or Toeplitz (whichever has a better fit by AICC value) within-subject variance-covariance matrix. The denominator degrees of freedom will be according to the method of Kenward-Roger.

To control for multiplicity of select analyses, Hochberg's procedure will be used to test the protocol designated primary endpoint (PDSS) as well as the key secondary endpoint CGI-S, which are not expected to be negatively correlated. Accordingly, if the largest p-value among these two endpoints (at the primary time point) does not exceed 0.05, then both endpoints will be considered statistically significant. If the largest p-value exceeds 0.05 and the smallest p-value does not exceed 0.025, then the endpoint with the smaller p-values will be considered statistically significant. This provides control of the familywise error rate at α = 0.05 such that either of the 2 endpoints statistically significant according to the above procedure will constitute a successful efficacy outcome for the trial.

Standard numeric descriptive statistics include number of patients or records observed, mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, and maximum values. Standard categorical descriptive statistics include the count and percentages of patients.

Assuming a standard deviation of 4.5 for the PDSS, 80 patients will provide more than 95% power to detect a difference in the mean change (from baseline) in the PDSS score of 3.75 at an alpha-level of 0.05 at 12 weeks.

attributes.text: Developed by Dogan and Caydam (2021), the scale consists of 26 items and 5 sub-dimensions (perceived susceptibility, perceived benefit, perceived severity, perceived barriers, and self-efficacy). The HBMSSC is a five-point Likert-type scale, and each item is answered from "disagree=1" to "strongly agree=5".
The total Cronbach's alpha coefficient of the scale is 0.86, and for the sub-dimensions it is 0.89; 0.79; 0.77; 0.65 and 0.86, respectively.

attributes.details: Part B uses adaptive Bayesian methodology. For anti-PD-(L)1 naive patients (B3, B4): predictive probability calculated after 12 patients to assess chance of observing ≥8 of 35 responses. Interim analysis at 20 patients if predictive probability ≥20%. Arms stopped if predictive probability <20%. For anti-PD-(L)1 pretreated patients (B1, B2): predictive probability for ≥3 of 20 responses after 10 patients, no formal interim analysis. Arm B8 incorporates futility monitoring beginning with 15th patient for chance of 13 responses in 48 patients.

attributes.n: Part A: ~30 evaluable patients per treatment arm for dose-escalation, ~18 for safety run-in, ~20 per tumor type for solid malignancy cohorts. Part B: 10-55 patients for B1-B6 depending on arm, 48 patients each for B7-B8
attributes.power: Not specified for efficacy. Operating characteristics: Part A CRM selects correct dose 50.9-60.1% of trials
attributes.assumptions: Part B: 9% probability of <12 responses given 35% true response rate for B7; 20% probability given 25% true response rate for B8

attributes.indication: Cancer immunotherapy trials

attributes.name: iCR (immune complete response)
attributes.definition: Complete response using iRECIST criteria - may occur after prior iUPD

attributes.name: iPR (immune partial response)
attributes.definition: Partial response using iRECIST criteria - may occur after prior iUPD

attributes.name: iSD (immune stable disease)
attributes.definition: Stable disease using iRECIST criteria - may occur after prior iUPD

attributes.name: iUPD (immune unconfirmed progression)
attributes.definition: Initial progression by RECIST 1.1 criteria requiring confirmation

attributes.name: iCPD (immune confirmed progression)
attributes.definition: Confirmed progression after iUPD showing further increase or new lesions

attributes.name: iPFS (immune progression-free survival)
attributes.definition: Time from treatment start to confirmed progression (iCPD) or death

attributes.name: iRECIST criteria
attributes.details: Modified RECIST 1.1 allowing for pseudoprogression patterns, requires confirmation of initial progression

attributes.name: RECIST 1.1
attributes.details: Standard response criteria - recommended to continue as primary for randomized licensing trials

attributes.event: First date of iUPD if subsequently confirmed as iCPD, or death
attributes.censoring: Censor if iUPD not confirmed and patient has subsequent iSD, iPR or iCR; censor if patient stops treatment due to clinical instability or no further assessments done

attributes.name: Clinically stable patients
attributes.definition: Patients with no worsening performance status, no clinically relevant increase in disease symptoms, no requirement for intensified symptom management after iUPD
